regime_context: Canada/TSX: The absolute-trend gate is validated for drawdown control; Big Banks lead with high durability but are crowded, while Base Metals emerges with zero breadth. Ineligible themes like Technology are gated out. The macro backdrop is dominated by unscheduled AI/geopolitics news (96% unscheduled share), implying high uncertainty.
emerging_watch: Base Metals & Copper (XBM.TO): condition to watch — daily breadth (fraction of constituents above 50-day MA) rises above 0.4 AND its momentum score surpasses Big Banks, which would indicate a confirmed handoff; currently breadth is 0.0 and margin is 0.54.

theses.subject: Big Banks
theses.thesis: Big Banks are the trend-eligible leader with broad participation (breadth=1.0) and high durability (bar 0.69), supported by the absolute-trend gate which historically reduces drawdown risk. Crowding (z=1.05) suggests sizing down, not avoidance.
evidence: absolute-trend gate validated as risk control
theses.dissent: Crowding and mixed Hurst raise mean-reversion risk; unscheduled macro shocks could trigger a sharp rotation away from banks.

falsifier.text: ZEB.TO lags S&P/TSX by more than 5% over 20 trading days

theses.subject: Technology
theses.thesis: Technology is ineligible under the absolute-trend gate, which historically avoids drawdowns. Negative momentum score (-0.600) and gate failure support an underweight despite high durability value, as the gate overrides.
evidence: absolute-trend gate historically reduces exposure to tail risk
theses.dissent: AI-themed news could spark a sharp rebound; the gate is a risk control, not a return predictor, so it may mistakenly suppress a strong bounce.

falsifier.text: XIT.TO outperforms S&P/TSX by more than 3% over 20 trading days

macro_narrative.note: market-level macro/policy/geo narrative flow; coincident, not per-theme, never a trigger
